instructions: Drain the jackfruit and rinse it well. Pat it dry with a clean towel, then cut off the tough core pieces and discard them.

In a large bowl, off the heat, stir together 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Add the jackfruit and toss until every piece is coated.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the jackfruit and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until it starts to take on color.
Pour in 3/4 cup of the BBQ sauce and 1/4 cup water. Stir, turn the heat down to low, cover, and cook for 20 minutes. Stir it once or twice.

Meanwhile, make the slaw dressing. In a medium bowl, mash half the avocado with 1 tbsp maple syrup, the juice of the lemon, and a pinch each of salt and pepper. Stir in water 1 tbsp at a time until it's a thick dressing you can pour.
Toss 2 cups of the coleslaw mix with the dressing and set it in the fridge.
Uncover the skillet and turn the heat up to medium-high. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and clings to the jackfruit. Pull apart any big pieces with two forks.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Pile the jackfruit onto the buns and top with the slaw and the last 1/4 cup of BBQ sauce.
method_notes: Minimalist Baker is the lead (young green jackfruit in water, a spice rub, BBQ sauce, simmered covered for about 20 minutes, then a hot finish for color). Delish Knowledge agrees on the method but sautes onion first and mashes the jackfruit; it has only 3 ratings, so it was read for comparison only. Adapted: the lead's roasted cashews are left out to keep the dish nut-free, and the buns and BBQ sauce are listed as vegan, so check labels.
